summary: Collect and verify related papers for the CyberCase paper mechanism (traceable analysis, locator, structured output)

items.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations (ALCE)
items.authors: Tianyu Gao, Howard Yen, Jiatong Yu, Danqi Chen
items.what_it_does: Benchmark for LLM answers with inline citations to retrieved passages; citation recall and precision are judged by an NLI model. Even the best models lacked complete citation support for half of their ELI5 answers.
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Closest evaluation precedent for our traceable claim rate: claims without a located citation are our rule-based counterpart of their citation-recall failures. Difference: they cite whole passages and judge entailment; we cite exact spans and only locate them.

items.title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models (AIS)
items.authors: Hannah Rashkin, Vitaly Nikolaev, Matthew Lamm, Lora Aroyo, Michael Collins, Dipanjan Das, Slav Petrov, Gaurav Singh Tomar, Iulia Turc, David Reitter
items.what_it_does: Defines attribution of generated text to an identified source and an evaluation framework (AIS) for it.
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Use their definition wherever the paper says 'grounded'; our 'verified' is weaker (located, not attributable-in-meaning). Note: the repo's author list omits David Reitter; Crossref (checked 2026-10-03) lists ten authors.

items.title: Attribute First, then Generate: Locally-attributable Grounded Text Generation
items.authors: Aviv Slobodkin, Eran Hirsch, Arie Cattan, Tal Schuster, Ido Dagan
items.what_it_does: Selects source spans first, plans sentences, then writes; the selected spans become concise citations that people verified faster.
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Design precedent only: settle and check an intermediate structure (our checked claims) before generating from it (judgement, template report). We do not reproduce the method: one reading call writes claims and quotes together. Book framing forbids claiming we reproduce it.

items.title: Learning Fine-Grained Grounded Citations for Attributed Large Language Models (FRONT)
items.authors: Lei Huang, Xiaocheng Feng, Weitao Ma, Yuxuan Gu, Weihong Zhong, Xiachong Feng, Weijiang Yu, Weihua Peng, Duyu Tang, Dandan Tu, Bing Qin
items.what_it_does: Trains a model to select supporting quotes before answering, then aligns the answer to the quotes with preference optimization.
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Quote-before-answer is prior work; we train nothing and call a hosted model through an API, checking its quotes after decoding. Excluded earlier in related_studies_modules.md because it needs training; useful as contrast.
items.repo_source: docs/research/openreview-system-contribution-2026-10-01.md (venue checked on ACL Anthology); not in the listed files; Crossref re-checked 2026-10-03

items.title: SelfCite: Self-Supervised Alignment for Context Attribution in Large Language Models
items.authors: Yung-Sung Chuang, Benjamin Cohen-Wang, Zejiang Shen, Zhaofeng Wu, Hu Xu, Xi Victoria Lin, James R. Glass, Shang-Wen Li, Wen-Tau Yih
items.what_it_does: Rewards citations by ablating the cited context (removing it or keeping only it) and uses the reward to select and train citations.
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Improves how citations are generated; we only check whether the model's quotations occur in the source, so it is not a verifier of meaning and not the same method.
items.repo_source: docs/research/openreview-system-contribution-2026-10-01.md (PMLR confirmed); not in the listed files; PMLR page re-read 2026-10-03

items.title: Verifiable by Design: Aligning Language Models to Quote from Pre-Training Data (Quote-Tuning)
items.authors: Jingyu Zhang, Marc Marone, Tianjian Li, Benjamin Van Durme, Daniel Khashabi
items.what_it_does: Tunes models to quote verbatim from pre-training data; quoting is measured by approximate corpus membership of 25-character n-grams (Bloom filter, QUIP), then DPO. NQ QUIP 34.9 to 54.5.
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Checking that model text occurs in a corpus is established; theirs is approximate membership over a pre-training corpus, ours is exact, source-specific location of each quote in the case sources. Their limitations note quotes do not guarantee usefulness.

items.title: EviReport: From Reasoned Outlines to Evidence Tracked Long-Form Reports
items.authors: Zihan Liu, Jianhui Li, Zexin Wang, Fei Sun, Jingjing Li, Zheyuan Li, Ke Xiang, Hang Cui, Houhua Gong, Changhua Pei, Gaogang Xie
items.what_it_does: Organises corpus evidence into traceable units, composes the report strictly from extracted facts, and scores factual accuracy and factual coverage separately (as described in the book draft).
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Same spirit: evidence tracked into the report, coverage reported beside accuracy. We report coverage beside traceability and build the report from a template. Owner asked for it beside ClinicalQuotes (book_framing).
items.repo_source: F:\Thesis\book_2026-10-01_planB\references.json (liu2026) and FRAMING_PASS_REPORT.md (checked on ACL Anthology); named in book_framing_2026-10-01.md; Crossref re-checked 2026-10-03

items.title: Can AI Validate Science? Benchmarking LLMs on Claim->Evidence Reasoning in AI Papers (CLAIM-BENCH)
items.authors: S. R. Javaji, Y. Cao, H. Li, Y. Yu, N. Muralidhar, Z. Zhu
items.what_it_does: LLMs extract claims and evidence with exact-quote fields from whole papers; single-pass recall falls with paper length (LLaMA-70B about 0.60 to 0.40 at 20k+ tokens), and three-pass or one-by-one strategies mostly remove the drop.
items.relation_to_us: [attribution] Closest published design to our claims-with-verbatim-quotes, and evidence that splitting the work recovers recall (our reading+judgement arm). It asks for exact quotes but the repo does not record a code-side occurrence check.

items.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
items.authors: Sewon Min, Kalpesh Krishna, Xinxi Lyu, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Pang Wei Koh, Mohit Iyyer, Luke Zettlemoyer, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
items.what_it_does: Splits generated text into atomic facts after generation and scores the share supported by a knowledge source; automated estimator within 2% of human judgement.
items.relation_to_us: [support] We move the splitting into the reading call (atomic claims with IDs). Unlike FActScore we do not judge support, only locate quotes; FActScore is the kind of support measure our paper leaves as future work.

items.title: SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization
items.authors: Philippe Laban, Tobias Schnabel, Paul N. Bennett, Marti A. Hearst
items.venue: Transactions of the ACL, vol. 10, pp. 163-177, doi:10.1162/tacl_a_00453
items.what_it_does: NLI-based detection of summary-source inconsistency applied at sentence granularity.
items.relation_to_us: [support] The NLI support check our locator deliberately does not perform; cite it when stating that 'verified' means located, not supported. The book audit lists it as an addition after Zhang et al.; no repo check recorded, metadata confirmed on Crossref 2026-10-03.

items.title: CogniBench: A Legal-inspired Framework and Dataset for Assessing Cognitive Faithfulness of Large Language Models
items.authors: Xiaqiang Tang, Jian Li, Keyu Hu, Nan Du, Xiaolong Li, Xi Zhang, Weigao Sun, Sihong Xie
items.what_it_does: Separates factual statements from cognitive (inferential) statements and builds criteria and data for judging the faithfulness of inferences.
items.relation_to_us: [support] Supports evaluating reported facts and inferences differently; our claims carry a type (reported / analytical inference) and status, but we do not check cognitive faithfulness.
items.repo_source: docs/research/openreview-system-contribution-2026-10-01.md (ACL Anthology); not in the listed files; Crossref re-checked 2026-10-03

items.title: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Large Language Models Through News Summarization
items.authors: D. Tam, A. Mascarenhas, S. Zhang, S. Kwan, M. Bansal, C. Raffel
items.what_it_does: Tests 23 LLMs on preferring consistent over inconsistent news summaries; the preference reverses when the inconsistent statement is copied verbatim from the source.
items.relation_to_us: [support] Direct reason why a verbatim, located quote is not evidence of a true or supported claim; also news-domain like CASIE.

items.title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
items.authors: C. Niu, Y. Wu, J. Zhu, S. Xu, K. Shum, R. Zhong, J. Song, T. Zhang
items.what_it_does: Word-level hallucination corpus for RAG outputs; unsupported and contradicted content persists even when relevant passages are supplied.
items.relation_to_us: [support] Supplying the source does not make output supported; motivates checking every quotation and keeping unlocated claims 'not confirmed'.

items.title: Zero-Shot Belief: A Hard Problem for LLMs
items.authors: John Murzaku, Owen Rambow
items.what_it_does: Shows LLMs struggle to predict zero-shot which source holds a belief about an event and how firmly.
items.relation_to_us: [support] Our claim epistemic status is a claim-level version of that label; only one status transition is checked by code (reported without a located quote becomes not_confirmed).

items.title: LLM Judges Verify Presence, Not Absence: Omission Blindness in AI Clinical Notes and What Recovers It
items.authors: Sebastian Fox, Luke Markham, Ryan Lail, Michael Karotsieris
items.what_it_does: LLM judges separate altered content well (0.79-0.94) but detect omissions barely above chance (0.50-0.63); enumerate-then-check recovers some.
items.relation_to_us: [support] Supports measuring coverage against independent gold event arguments (CASIE) instead of an LLM judge, since omission is the main failure of long structured output.

items.title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
items.authors: Ziwei Ji, Nayeon Lee, Rita Frieske, Tiezheng Yu, et al.
items.what_it_does: Survey and terminology for hallucination in NLG.
items.relation_to_us: [support] Terminology source for intrinsic/extrinsic hallucination when describing what the locator does and does not catch.

items.title: Improving Faithfulness of Large Language Models in Summarization via Sliding Generation and Self-Consistency (SliSum)
items.authors: T. Li, Z. Li, Y. Zhang
items.what_it_does: Summarises overlapping windows of a long document and keeps only content several windows agree on.
items.relation_to_us: [support] A model-side faithfulness fix for long inputs; contrast with our code-side quote check. Low priority.

items.title: Verifiable by Construction: Claim-Level Evaluation of Verbatim Citation in Clinical Question Answering
items.authors: Jiashuo Zhang, Yuling Chen, Yvonne Commodore-Mensah, Michael Oberst
items.what_it_does: 12 models answer 222 clinical questions with guideline quotes; deterministic verbatim check (exact, normalized Unicode/case/quotes/dashes/whitespace/markup, elided fragments of 10+ chars), then an LLM judge for support. claude-opus-5: 100% VCR but 37.1% of claims fully supported.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] Closest prior art: our locator tiers match theirs almost tier for tier, so the locator is not novel. [support] Their result is why we say 'verifiable, not verified-as-true'; support is our future work.

items.title: Verifying LLM Citations with Pydantic (Instructor blog; CitationMixin / exact citations example)
items.authors: Jason Liu
items.venue: Instructor documentation blog, 18 Nov 2023 (grey literature, not peer-reviewed)
items.what_it_does: Validates that model-quoted spans exist in the context: exact match, then a normalized match (lower case, collapsed whitespace), mapping offsets back so the stored quote is an exact slice of the source.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] The core of our locator is established practice since 2023 (owner correction 2026-10-01). Our additions (NFKC, ellipsis pieces, markup-tolerant and format-only tiers, multi-source locators, demotion, near-match pointer) are application-specific, not new.

items.title: The theory and computation of evolutionary distances: Pattern recognition
items.authors: Peter H. Sellers
items.what_it_does: Approximate pattern matching: edit distance of a pattern against the best-matching substring of a text (infix / semi-global alignment).
items.relation_to_us: [locate] The algorithmic basis of the near-match pointer's infix edit distance that finds the nearest source passage for an unlocated quote. Named in the book audit as a preliminary; no repo check recorded; Crossref checked 2026-10-03.

items.title: Identification of common molecular subsequences
items.authors: T. F. Smith, M. S. Waterman
items.venue: Journal of Molecular Biology 147(1), pp. 195-197, doi:10.1016/0022-2836(81)90087-5
items.what_it_does: Local sequence alignment algorithm.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] Local alignment precedent for aligning a near-miss quote with its nearest passage; named with Passim in the book audit. No repo check recorded; Crossref checked 2026-10-03.

items.title: Computational Methods for Uncovering Reprinted Texts in Antebellum Newspapers
items.authors: David A. Smith, Ryan Cordell, Abby Mullen
items.venue: American Literary History 27(3), pp. E1-E15, doi:10.1093/alh/ajv029
items.what_it_does: Text-reuse detection over noisy newspaper text (the Passim approach): candidate passages by n-gram matching, then local alignment.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] Same two-step shape as our pointer (rapidfuzz candidates, then infix edit distance). The audit names 'Passim with Smith-Waterman' but no specific paper; this identification and the method summary are mine and must be confirmed against the full text before citing. Metadata from Crossref 2026-10-03.

items.title: Self-Verification Improves Few-Shot Clinical Information Extraction
items.authors: Zelalem Gero, Chandan Singh, Hao Cheng, Tristan Naumann, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao, Hoifung Poon
items.what_it_does: The LLM gives a short provenance span for each extracted item so experts can audit it, and self-verifies its output.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] Closest to our quotations in clinical IE; the repo notes the full text was not read, so whether their spans are string-checked against the note is unknown. We check by code, not by the model.

items.title: Large language models are few-shot clinical information extractors
items.authors: Monica Agrawal, Stefan Hegselmann, Hunter Lang, Yoon Kim, David Sontag
items.what_it_does: Uses GPT-3 for clinical IE with resolvers that map free LM output back to the label space; distils into smaller models because of size and privacy.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] Each LLM-for-IE system adds a step tying output back to text or labels; our locator is that step, done by code against the source. Also supports the open-weight/privacy property (write it as a property, not the original reason).

items.title: GPT-NER: Named Entity Recognition via Large Language Models
items.authors: Shuhe Wang, Xiaofei Sun, Xiaoya Li, Rongbin Ouyang, Fei Wu, Tianwei Zhang, Jiwei Li, Guoyin Wang, Chen Guo
items.what_it_does: Recasts NER as LLM generation; adds LLM self-verification because the model over-labels null inputs.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] Model-side verification of extracted items versus our code-side location of quotes. Repo records only 'Wang et al.'; full author list from Crossref 2026-10-03.

items.title: Time for aCTIon: Automated Analysis of Cyber Threat Intelligence in the Wild
items.authors: Giuseppe Siracusano, Davide Sanvito, Roberto Gonzalez, Manikantan Srinivasan, Sivakaman Kamatchi, Wataru Takahashi, Masaru Kawakita, Takahiro Kakumaru, Roberto Bifulco
items.what_it_does: LLM answers one question per STIX entity type and code assembles the bundle; a string check found 2 invented entities (0.9%) while the LLM self-check found none.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] Security-domain evidence that a code string check catches inventions an LLM self-check misses; checks entity names, not quotations.

items.title: From Judgments to Issues: Structured Extraction of Legal Reasoning with Citation-Hallucination Control
items.authors: Giovanni Piccioli, Alessia Fidelangeli, Piera Santin, Pierpaolo Vivo
items.what_it_does: Prompt-only DeepSeek V3 extracts issues from long judgments (split into two calls); 31 of 264 citations (11.7%) hallucinated before a citation filter, 0.9% after, with 7 valid ones (3.0%) removed.
items.relation_to_us: [locate] A filter on model citations in a long structured extraction, with its false-removal cost reported; our near-match pointer avoids silent removal by showing the nearest passage to a person.

items.title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Large Language Model Performance
items.authors: Zhi Rui Tam, Cheng-Kuang Wu, Yi-Lin Tsai, Chieh-Yen Lin, Hung-yi Lee, Yun-Nung Chen
items.what_it_does: Format restrictions (JSON mode etc.) lowered reasoning accuracy, more so when stricter; JSON mode put the answer key before the reason key. Contested by the .txt blog 'Say What You Mean'.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Quality side of grammar vs free decoding; the literature disagrees, and our 2x2 measures reliability and coverage, not reasoning accuracy.

items.title: JSONSchemaBench: A Rigorous Benchmark of Structured Outputs for Language Models
items.authors: Saibo Geng, Hudson Cooper, Michal Moskal, Samuel Jenkins, Julian Berman, Nathan Ranchin, Robert West, Eric Horvitz, Harsha Nori
items.what_it_does: 10K schemas, six constrained-decoding frameworks incl. XGrammar; constrained decoding raised task accuracy; failure modes listed are compile errors, timeouts, over/under-constraint.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Does not discuss whitespace runaway; positions our measured reliability cost as the side it does not cover. Full author list from arXiv API 2026-10-03 (repo records 'Geng et al.').

items.title: Correctness-Guaranteed Code Generation via Constrained Decoding
items.authors: Li, Rahili, Zhao
items.what_it_does: Constrained decoder for code; states that nontermination is a well-known issue of constrained decoding (distribution distortion) and counts runs over 1,500 tokens as failures.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Peer-reviewed statement that the failure we measured (runaway under a grammar) is known; it gives no rate, we give one in a deployed application.

items.title: TruncProof: A Guardrail for LLM-based JSON Generation under Token-Length Constraints
items.authors: Kato, Tarashima
items.venue: IJCNN 2026 per arXiv comment (self-reported; no Xplore record found yet); arXiv 2605.13076
items.what_it_does: Grammar constraints cannot enforce a token limit; baselines (Outlines, SynCode, XGrammar) reach 1-36% syntax accuracy under tight limits; attribute waste to excessive whitespace; LL(1) logit modifier fixes it inside the decoder.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Closest peer-reviewed support for 'whitespace exhausts the budget under grammar'. Differences: they control the engine and use tight budgets on short JSON; we call a hosted model through a router with a generous budget and fix it in the application.

items.title: Guiding LLMs The Right Way: Fast, Non-Invasive Constrained Generation (DOMINO)
items.authors: Luca Beurer-Kellner, Marc Fischer, Martin Vechev
items.what_it_does: Subword tokens misalign with grammar boundaries; careless constraining distorts output and lowers accuracy.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Mechanism behind why the grammar-constrained reading drifted into whitespace and corrupted typographic characters in quotes.

items.title: Grammar-Aligned Decoding
items.authors: Kanghee Park, Jiayu Wang, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Nadia Polikarpova, Loris D'Antoni
items.what_it_does: Shows grammar-constrained decoding distorts the model distribution: outputs stay grammatical but are improbable under the model.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] General mechanism for masked closing braces leaving whitespace as the only legal continuation.

items.title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
items.authors: Yixin Dong, Charlie F. Ruan, Yaxing Cai, Ruihang Lai, Ziyi Xu, Yilong Zhao, Tianqi Chen
items.venue: arXiv 2411.15100 (arXiv comment says MLSys '25; book references.json cites the arXiv version)
items.what_it_does: Structured-generation engine that masks invalid tokens; the library default allows unbounded whitespace.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] The engine likely behind our providers' JSON-schema mode; cite when stating the mechanism (unbounded whitespace) and that a router user cannot change engine settings.

items.title: Lost in Space: Finding the Right Tokens for Structured Output
items.authors: Sil Hamilton, David Mimno
items.what_it_does: Whitespace choices in the output format change accuracy by 5-10%; leading whitespace helps smaller models.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Whitespace in structured output is not neutral; context for our whitespace runaway.

items.title: Constrained Decoding Eliminates Structural Failures in Small LLMs but Reveals a Scale-Dependent Semantic Gap
items.authors: Akash Chavan
items.what_it_does: Five 0.6-4B models under Outlines and XGrammar reach 100% schema validity; truncation, runaway and cost are not measured.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Shows validity-only evaluation misses what we measure (failed cases, calls to the cap, seconds, USD).

items.title: When JSON Is Not Enough: Semantic Reliability of Schema-Constrained LLM Ordering Agents
items.authors: Yin Li
items.what_it_does: 2,400 calls on a hosted provider against provider JSON schema (GPT-OSS 120B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-2B); 100% validity, no truncation or runaway reported.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Counter-example: a hosted stack does not always show the failure, so our decoding result must be scoped to model, provider stack and long outputs.

items.title: The Hidden Cost of Structured Generation in LLMs: Draft-Conditioned Constrained Decoding
items.authors: A. Reddy, T. T. Walker, J. S. Ide, A. S. Bedi
items.what_it_does: Decode-time masking alone costs 9.4-27.6 points on MATH500; drafting first and constraining after recovers most of it. Small outputs only.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Supports drafting freely and enforcing structure afterwards, which is our reading call (prompt-described JSON, validated after decoding).

items.title: Stay Within Your Bounds: Distance-Guided Decoding for Guaranteed Context-Free Grammar Compliance (SWYB)
items.authors: V. Collura, K. Tit, E. Giunchiglia, M. Papadakis, M. Cordy
items.what_it_does: Names 'budget saturation': local masking keeps every prefix completable but gives no signal to stop; prunes tokens whose distance to completion exceeds the remaining budget.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Peer-reviewed name for the mechanism we observe; their fix is inside the decoder, ours is in the application. No whitespace-loop data.

items.title: Closed-Loop Validation-Repair for Healthcare Interoperability: A Multi-Model Study of Schema Compliance in Clinical LLMs
items.authors: J. Shen
items.what_it_does: A deterministic validator feeds field-level errors back for up to 3 repairs: 89.0% to 99.0% compliance, all converging by round two, 1.11-1.20 calls per case. Short records.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Supports our bound of re-asking at most twice after validation; theirs is short records, ours multi-thousand-token traces.

items.title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark and Evaluation Methodology for Complex Structured Extraction
items.authors: Nick Ferguson, Josh Pennington, Narek Beghian, Aravind Mohan, Douwe Kiela, Sheshansh Agrawal, Thien Hang Nguyen
items.venue: arXiv 2602.12247 (preprint; KDD '26 template with placeholder DOI, acceptance unconfirmed)
items.what_it_does: Schemas of 13-369 keys, gold outputs up to ~25k tokens; prompt mode 107/210 valid vs provider structured-output mode 77/210; failure attributed to output volume.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Independent evidence that provider structured-output mode can lower validity for large outputs, matching our grammar-vs-validation result. Name collision with the LlamaIndex ExtractBench: cite with authors.

items.title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction
items.authors: Boyang Zhang, Adrian Lyjak, Eli Stewart, Zhaoqi Li, Simon Suo
items.venue: arXiv 2607.29677 (technical report; the authors' product ranks first)
items.what_it_does: On long documents value F1 collapses (Gemini 3.5 Flash 87.9 to 27.9) as a recall failure (P 83.7 vs R 26.5), attributed to systems stopping early.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Omission, not wrong values, dominates long structured output; motivates our coverage of gold facts beside traceability.

items.title: SO-Bench: A Structural Output Evaluation of Multimodal LLMs
items.authors: Di Feng, Kaixin Ma, Feng Nan, Haofeng Chen, Bohan Zhai, David Griffiths, Mingfei Gao, Zhe Gan, Eshan Verma, Yinfei Yang, Zhifeng Chen, Afshin Dehghan
items.what_it_does: Schemas up to depth 22 and 2K+ fields; structured-output API gave lower field match than prompting for all six API models (e.g., GPT-5 62.67 vs 64.52).
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Another measurement where provider structured output underperforms prompt + parse.

items.title: StructuredRAG: JSON Response Formatting with Large Language Models
items.authors: Connor Shorten, Charles Pierse, Thomas Benjamin Smith, Erika Cardenas, Akanksha Sharma, John Trengrove, Bob van Luijt
items.what_it_does: Prompted JSON fails even when tiny: 82.55% average success, lists of objects 67.6%; most common failure is chatter before the JSON.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Why prompt-described JSON needs validation after decoding and a re-ask.

items.title: DeepJSONEval: Benchmarking Complex Nested JSON Data Mining for Large Language Models
items.authors: Zhicheng Zhou, Jing Li, Suming Qiu, Junjie Huang, Linyuan Qiu, Zhijie Sun
items.what_it_does: Depth 3-4 to 5-7 drops strict match 17.22-37.53%; response length barely correlates with failure.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Counterpoint on whether depth or volume drives failure; our trace is shallow but long. Repo warns not to state whether constrained decoding was used.

items.title: LongProc: Benchmarking Long-Context Language Models on Long Procedural Generation
items.authors: X. Ye, F. Yin, Y. He, J. Zhang, H. Yen, T. Gao, G. Durrett, D. Chen
items.what_it_does: Scores fall as the output budget grows: GPT-4o 94.8 / 83.4 / 38.1 at 0.5K / 2K / 8K output tokens.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Long outputs degrade; our reading writes 5-15k-token JSON, which motivates splitting reading from judgement. Output is TSV/procedural text, not JSON.

items.title: DocETL: Agentic Query Rewriting and Evaluation for Complex Document Processing
items.authors: S. Shankar, T. Chambers, T. Shah, A. G. Parameswaran, E. Wu
items.what_it_does: Splitting a 41-type contract extraction into 21 calls raised recall 0.430 to 0.719 and removed hallucinated categories, at about 18x cost.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Decomposition raises recall at a cost; our two-call design is the cheap end (two calls) and we report cost.

items.title: MatViX: Multimodal Information Extraction from Visually Rich Articles
items.authors: G. Khalighinejad, S. Scott, O. Liu, K. L. Anderson, R. Stureborg, A. Tyagi, B. Dhingra
items.what_it_does: Staged extraction (text, then figures, then merge) because one whole-paper call worked worse; recall far below precision for every model.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Another staged-vs-single result; cite the NAACL tables (numbers differ from arXiv v1).

items.title: Overview of the CRF 2026 Shared Task on Clinical Case Report Forms Filling
items.authors: P. Ferrazzi, S. Ghosh, A. Lavelli, B. Magnini
items.what_it_does: 134 items per note, ~95% unknown; grouped extractors (68.3 macro-F1) beat one all-items call (52.4) and per-item baseline (47.0); errors are unsupported filled values.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Supports splitting one big extraction call; also warns a re-ask must not force every field to be filled.

items.title: MulitaMiner: A Multi-Version Evaluation of LLM-Based Vulnerability Report Extraction
items.authors: B. Machado, D. Lautert, C. Kapelinski, D. Kreutz, I. Garcia Ferrao, A. Bof
items.what_it_does: Scanner PDF reports to 18-field records with schema in the prompt, JSON repair and up to 3 retries; omission fell 20.5% to 1.7% across versions while hallucination stayed ~6-7%; GPT-5 omitted 66-81% when reasoning used up the output budget.
items.relation_to_us: [structure] Security-domain precedent for prompt-described JSON plus validation and retries; measure omission and hallucination separately, as we separate coverage from traceability.

items.title: From Legacy to Standard: LLM-Assisted Transformation of Cybersecurity Playbooks into CACAO Format
items.authors: M. Akbari Gurabi, L. Nitz, R.-M. Castravet, R. Matzutt, A. Mandal, S. Decker
items.venue: ESORICS 2025 International Workshops, LNCS, Springer 2026, pp. 491-510, doi:10.1007/978-3-032-16092-8_27

items.authors: Y. Cheng, O. Bajaber, S. A. Tsegai, D. Song, P. Gao

items.title: Decompose, Enrich, and Extract! Schema-aware Event Extraction using LLMs

items.authors: Diana Kramer, Lambert Rosique, Ajay Narotam, Elie Bursztein, Patrick Gage Kelley, Kurt Thomas, Allison Woodruff

items.title: Forensic Schema for Psychological Manipulation in Cyber Fraud: LLM-Driven Victim Reports Analysis
items.authors: Zikai Alex Wen, Corrazon Ogot, Juan Li, Yan Bai

items.title: Structured Report Generation using Local LLMs for Chat-Based Digital Forensics
items.authors: Ying Dehing, Hans Henseler, Timo Meconi, Marcel Worring, Harm van Beek

items.relation_to_us: [domain] Staged forensic analysis with ID-level traceability exists; we check verbatim quotations against sources and evaluate against independent human gold (CASIE).
